## Reading
- **Compulsory:** @strogatz2024nonlinear, Section 3.7, "Insect outbreak".
- **Recommended:** @ludwig1978qualitative.

The spruce budworm is a forest insect whose outbreaks defoliate balsam fir forests. Ludwig, Jones and Holling modelled the budworm and forest system of New Brunswick, Canada, with the budworm as a fast variable and the forest as a slow one [@ludwig1978qualitative]. On this page you keep the forest fixed and study the budworm alone, as in @strogatz2024nonlinear, Section 3.7.

## The dimensional model

Let $N(t)$ be the budworm density. With the forest held fixed,

$$
\frac{dN}{dt} = RN\left(1 - \frac{N}{K}\right) - \frac{BN^2}{A^2 + N^2}.
$$ {#eq-budworm-dimensional}

- $RN(1 - N/K)$ is logistic growth with rate $R$ and carrying capacity $K$. The carrying capacity depends on the amount of foliage.
- $p(N) = BN^2/(A^2 + N^2)$ is predation, mainly by birds. It saturates at the maximum rate $B$ when budworms are abundant. It vanishes like $N^2$ at low density, because birds switch to other food when budworms are rare. This is a Holling type III functional response [@ludwig1978qualitative, p. 317].
- $A$ sets the density at which predation starts to saturate: $p(A) = B/2$.

Ludwig et al. chose these forms because they need few parameters, and they state that the conclusions depend only on the qualitative shape of the terms [@ludwig1978qualitative, p. 317].

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-predation
#| fig-cap: "Type III predation term p(N)/B as a function of N/A. It is small at low density and saturates at 1."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 6, 400)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
ax.plot(x, x**2 / (1 + x**2))
ax.axhline(1, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1)
ax.axvline(1, color="gray", ls=":", lw=1)
ax.set_xlabel("N / A")
ax.set_ylabel("p(N) / B")
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Removing the units

@eq-budworm-dimensional has four parameters $R, K, A, B$. Rescale the density by $A$ and time by $A/B$:

$$
x = \frac{N}{A}, \qquad \tau = \frac{B}{A}t .
$$

Since $dN/dt = B\, dx/d\tau$, dividing @eq-budworm-dimensional by $B$ gives

$$
\frac{dx}{d\tau} = r x\left(1 - \frac{x}{k}\right) - \frac{x^2}{1 + x^2},
\qquad
r = \frac{RA}{B}, \quad k = \frac{K}{A}.
$$ {#eq-budworm}

Only two dimensionless groups remain [@strogatz2024nonlinear, Section 3.7]. Ludwig et al. obtain the same groups under the names $R$ and $Q$ [@ludwig1978qualitative, eqn 8].

- $r$ compares the budworm growth rate with the maximum predation rate.
- $k$ is the carrying capacity measured in units of the predation scale $A$.

The rest of the module uses @eq-budworm. Parameter values quoted as $r$ and $k$ are always the dimensionless ones.

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise
Check that $r$ and $k$ are dimensionless. Assume $N$ is measured in larvae per acre and $t$ in years.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$R$ has units 1/year. $A$ has units larvae/acre. $B$ is a rate of larvae eaten, so it has units larvae/acre/year. Then $RA/B$ has units (1/year)(larvae/acre)/(larvae/acre/year), which cancel. $K/A$ is a ratio of two densities.
:::
